items.title: Shelly Berg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: you can put on your Will Lee bass loop and your Peter Erskine drum loop

ctx.x: Do you think the tools that are available today — how should I say this — don’t foster that kind of ability?

It’s a concern. It’s great in that you can immediately hear in terms of trial and error and learning to hear and getting to hear back what you’ve written. It’s a great tool, with the caveat that you’re not really hearing back what you’ve written. And chances are it may sound a whole lot better or a whole lot worse in a real environment. So there’s certainly some use to it. I find in the industry now everybody wants a full demo of any orchestra piece you write. And you can get it to sound so good that they think…
years ago could never have been in this business. And it becomes hard to separate them out.
